findings.title: verify does not honor session expiry
findings.description: Authenticator::verify returns a session for any known token without checking expires_at, so expired sessions remain valid.

findings.title: require_admin always returns false
findings.description: The condition uses OR between two inequality checks, so it is true for every role and no session can ever pass.

findings.title: bearer_token can overflow or dereference null
findings.description: It copies the header into a fixed 64-byte buffer and assumes a space exists, causing buffer overflow or a null-pointer dereference for malformed or missing Authorization headers.

findings.title: Cache leaks Entry objects
findings.description: Entry objects are allocated with new but are not deleted on eviction, expiry, overwrite, sweep, or destruction; entries_ only stores raw pointers.

findings.title: sweep invalidates its iterator while erasing
findings.description: The loop increments the iterator after entries_.erase(it), which is undefined behavior.

findings.title: utilization uses integer division and can divide by zero
findings.description: entries_.size() / limit_ is usually zero, and a cache limit of zero causes division by zero.

findings.title: Cache eviction does not implement LRU
findings.description: The documented eviction policy is least recently used, but set always erases entries_.begin(), which is ordered by code rather than access time.

findings.title: validate always reports success
findings.description: validate collects problems but unconditionally returns true, so invalid configurations pass startup validation.

findings.title: bad LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS is still applied
findings.description: When the parsed timeout is zero, the function logs the bad value but still sets cfg.timeout to zero instead of keeping the default.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but ignored
findings.description: The parsed value is cast to void and cfg.fetch_limit is never updated.

findings.title: cache TTL milliseconds are treated as seconds
findings.description: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is documented as milliseconds, but it is directly converted to Seconds without scaling, producing durations thousands of times too long.

findings.title: format_row returns a dangling pointer
findings.description: It returns a pointer to a local automatic array that no longer exists after the function returns.

findings.title: report reads the wrong file name
findings.description: export_csv turns an empty name into links.csv, but read_report is called with the original empty name and looks for .csv.

findings.title: write_snapshot renames before flushing output
findings.description: std::rename is called while the ofstream may still hold buffered data, so bytes may not be on disk before the rename.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: errors_ has no default initializer, so Metrics::errors() returns an indeterminate value.

findings.title: quotas exposes a mutable store reference
findings.description: The API promises a snapshot, but it returns a non-const reference that lets callers mutate the store's quota map.

findings.title: stats divides by the store size without checking for zero
findings.description: When the store is empty, g_store->total_hits() / g_store->size() performs division by zero.

findings.title: request handlers dereference missing query values
findings.description: create_link and other handlers use std::map::at without handling missing parameters, causing uncaught exceptions on malformed requests.

findings.title: resolve deletes live links and accepts expired ones
findings.description: The expiry test is inverted, so active links are erased while expired links continue to resolve.

findings.title: rename validates the source code twice
findings.description: validate_code is called twice on from and never on to, so an invalid target code is not checked.

findings.title: page computes an out-of-range end index
findings.description: end is set to all.size() + 1 when it exceeds the vector size, causing construction past end() and undefined behavior.

findings.title: success_rate truncates before scaling
findings.description: used / links_.size() * 100 evaluates integer division first, yielding 0 unless every link has been used.

findings.title: remove does not refund the owner quota
findings.description: The link is erased but quota_[owner] is not decremented, contradicting the documented behavior.

findings.title: top sorts ascending and may append default links
findings.description: It sorts by ascending hits and calls resize(n), which value-initializes extra links when n exceeds the number of entries.

findings.title: by_owner matches owners by substring
findings.description: owner.find(owner) accepts any owner containing the query, rather than requiring an exact owner match.

findings.title: extend revives expired links
findings.description: It unconditionally moves expiry into the future even for links whose expiry was supposed to be final.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic
findings.description: Links are inserted while validation is still in progress, so a later invalid code leaves partial state behind.

findings.title: prune invalidates its iterator and returns the wrong count
findings.description: It increments after erasing and returns links_.size() instead of the number removed.

findings.title: last_code returns a dangling view and picks the wrong link
findings.description: It constructs a temporary string and returns a view into it, and map iteration selects the last key rather than the most recently created link.

findings.title: janitor loop invalidates its iterator while erasing
findings.description: store.all().erase(it) is called in a for loop that also increments it, which is undefined behavior.

findings.title: warm_cache returns before workers finish
findings.description: Spawned threads are never joined, violating the documented return-after-all-probes contract and leaving references at risk.

findings.title: check_targets reads past the end of the vector
findings.description: The loop uses <= links.size(), so it accesses links[links.size()], which is out of bounds.

findings.title: Janitor thread mutates store.all() without locking and invalidates iterators
findings.description: The janitor constructs a range-for over store.all() and calls store.all().erase(it) inside the loop, then performs ++it on an erased iterator. It runs concurrently with request-thread Store operations and Cache::sweep, so iteration and mutation race, expired entries can be skipped or mishandled, and container corruption is possible.

findings.title: warm_cache spawns std::thread workers that are never joined
findings.description: Workers are pushed into a vector but never joined, so vector destruction calls std::terminate. The lambda captures &link, whose lifetime is only the current range-for iteration, so a still-running worker can read a destroyed reference.

findings.title: Store maps are accessed concurrently without synchronization
findings.description: links_ and quota_ are mutated and iterated by request handlers and the janitor on different threads with no mutex. In addition all() returns a mutable map reference and quotas() returns a mutable map reference, exposing protected state to unsynchronized callers such as the janitor and admin_quotas.

findings.title: Cache entries map and hits counter lack synchronization
findings.description: get/set/erase/peek/sweep/utilization touch entries_ and hits_ concurrently from handler threads, janitor, and warm_cache workers. This is a data race with potential map corruption and use-after-free of Entry* (neither set nor erase frees evicted entries).

findings.title: Authenticator sessions map unprotected and verify returns dangling pointer
findings.description: issue and revoke mutate sessions_ while verify iterates it on other threads (data race). verify returns &pair.second, which can be invalidated by a later insert or erase, so handlers dereferencing the returned Session* may use freed memory.

findings.title: Metrics counters incremented and read without atomicity or initialization
findings.description: add_resolved/add_created use plain long increments and stats() reads them concurrently from multiple handler threads, causing lost updates and a data race. errors_ is also uninitialized, so stats() can read an indeterminate value.

findings.title: stop_janitor does not join the janitor thread
findings.description: stop_janitor only sets g_running to false and returns, leaving g_janitor possibly still running and undestroyed. The thread can outlive the objects it references (use-after-free at shutdown) and g_janitor is leaked.

findings.title: Falls back to a hard-coded, publicly known default secret
findings.description: When LINKD_SECRET is unset, Authenticator uses the literal "dev-secret-do-not-use" as its secret. Any deployment that forgets to set the variable runs with a published credential.

findings.title: Session tokens are generated with std::rand
findings.description: Tokens are minted from two std::rand() calls, which is not a cryptographically secure source. Predictable state lets an attacker guess or brute-force live session tokens.

findings.title: Issued session tokens are logged in plaintext
findings.description: issue() prints the full token to stdout, leaking credentials to logs that may be readable by operators or shipped to log aggregators.

findings.title: verify() does not check session expiration
findings.description: The function searches sessions_ and returns a pointer whenever the token matches, but never compares Clock::now() against expires_at, so expired sessions remain valid forever.

findings.title: require_admin() always returns false
findings.description: The condition uses || between two 'not equal' comparisons, which is true for every possible role, so the function rejects admin and owner alike and no privileged operation can succeed.

findings.title: Password hashing uses a weak, non-collision-resistant hash
findings.description: hash_password implements djb2 and truncates the result, providing no memory-hardness or cryptographic strength and inviting offline cracking/collisions.

findings.title: bearer_token overflows a fixed stack buffer and dereferences a null pointer
findings.description: header is copied into a 64-byte stack buffer with strcpy (overflow for long headers) and strchr's result is used without a null check, so a header without a space crashes the process.

findings.title: secret_equals has a (theoretical) timing side channel
findings.description: It returns early on the first mismatched byte and on differing lengths, leaking information about the secret through timing. The docstring claims no leakage.

findings.title: Cache destructor leaks Entry objects and expired entries
findings.description: entries_ holds raw Entry* pointers allocated with new; clear() only removes map nodes, never deleting them. Every swept/expired/overwritten entry is leaked.

findings.title: peek() reports expired entries as cached
findings.description: peek simply checks map membership and never consults expires, so callers see stale presence after TTL expiry.

findings.title: set() does not evict the LRU entry and leaks on overwrite
findings.description: Eviction always removes entries_.begin() (ordered by code, not recency), and overwriting an existing code replaces the pointer without deleting the old Entry. It also never updates an existing entry in place.

findings.title: sweep() erases while iterating, causing undefined behavior
findings.description: The loop calls entries_.erase(it) and then increments it, which is iterator invalidation. The janitor calls this every tick.

findings.title: utilization() divides before multiplying and may divide by zero
findings.description: entries_.size() / limit_ is integer division that yields 0 until the cache is full, and limit_ == 0 crashes.

findings.title: LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS (milliseconds) is treated as seconds
findings.description: The code sets cfg.timeout = Seconds{ms} even though the variable and comment say milliseconds, so a 10000 ms configuration becomes ~2.8 hours.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS (milliseconds) is treated as seconds
findings.description: cfg.cache_ttl = Seconds{atoi(ttl)} applies the raw millisecond value as seconds, inflating the TTL by 1000x.

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT is parsed but never applied
findings.description: parsed is computed and then discarded with (void)parsed, so fetch_limit always stays at the default 32.

findings.title: validate() returns true even when problems are found
findings.description: The function collects problems and prints them but unconditionally returns true, so invalid configuration passes startup (and main() ignores the result anyway).

findings.title: Path traversal in report name (export_csv/read_report)
findings.description: name is concatenated into a filesystem path with no sanitization, so values like '../etc/passwd' escape export_dir.

findings.title: Export file is world-readable despite the comment
findings.description: The ofstream is created with default permissions (typically 0644), contradicting the claim that only the service user may read it.

findings.title: archive_all builds paths from owner names
findings.description: Pair keys (owners) are used directly in file paths, allowing traversal/special characters, and write failures are silently ignored.

findings.title: write_snapshot uses a predictable /tmp path (TOCTOU/symlink)
findings.description: The temporary file is fixed at /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json and std::rename'd without fsync, enabling symlink attacks and not actually guaranteeing durability.

findings.title: format_row returns a dangling pointer to a stack buffer
findings.description: It returns char* pointing at local array row[128], which goes out of scope immediately, an undefined-behavior use-after-scope.

findings.title: CORS allows credentials with a wildcard origin
findings.description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, an invalid and insecure configuration.

findings.title: delete_link does not enforce ownership (IDOR)
findings.description: The comment says only the owner may delete, but remove() is called without verifying the session's owner, so any authenticated user can delete any link.

findings.title: Open redirect via user-controlled next parameter
findings.description: out() sets Location: to the raw ?next= value with no allow-list, enabling phishing/open redirect.

findings.title: Admin quota check trusts a client-supplied header
findings.description: admin_quotas only checks x-admin == "true" instead of the authenticated session's role, so any user can impersonate an admin.

findings.title: stats() divides by zero when the store is empty
findings.description: per_link = total_hits() / size() crashes on an empty store, a realistic startup state.

findings.title: report() uses a different name for the empty case
findings.description: export_csv() defaults an empty name to "links", but read_report() is called with the original empty name, reading "/dir/.csv" from a nonexistent path.

findings.title: Unknown token is echoed back in the 401 response
findings.description: The error body includes the presented token, leaking credentials into responses/logs.

findings.title: resolve() inverts the expiry check
findings.description: A link is erased and treated as missing while it is still valid, and expired links are served (and hit-counted). This both drops live data and revives dead codes.

findings.title: rename() uses a dangling reference after erase
findings.description: After links_.erase(it), the reference Link& link = it->second is dangling, yet its fields are read/written. It also validates `from` twice instead of `to`.

findings.title: page() computes an out-of-bounds end index
findings.description: end is set to all.size() + 1 when it exceeds size, so the returned view [offset, end) reads past the vector.

findings.title: success_rate() truncates to zero via integer division
findings.description: used / links_.size() * 100 divides before multiplying, yielding 0 for any used < size, so the reported rate is almost always 0.

findings.title: remove() neither refunds quota nor cleans cache
findings.description: The comment promises the owner's quota slot is returned, but quota_ (and any cache entry) is left inconsistent, leaking capacity.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending and pads the result with default-constructed links
findings.description: It sorts a.hits < b.hits (least first) then resize(n); when n exceeds available links, resize() appends empty Link objects.

findings.title: by_owner() uses substring matching instead of equality
findings.description: owner.find(owner) matches any owner containing the query as a substring, leaking unrelated owners' links.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links
findings.description: It unconditionally resets expires_at to now + ttl even for dead links, contrary to the documented invariant that expiry is final.

findings.title: quotas() returns a mutable reference to internal state
findings.description: The public API exposes quota_ for unrestricted mutation, violating the documented snapshot semantics; cache.cpp/main.cpp also mutate it via this ref.

findings.title: import_all is not atomic
findings.description: It inserts links one by one without rollback, so a validation failure mid-batch leaves a partial store despite the documented all-or-nothing contract.

findings.title: prune() invalidates its iterator and returns the wrong count
findings.description: It erases through `it` and then increments it (undefined behavior), and returns links_.size() instead of the number removed.

findings.title: last_code() returns the map-last key, not the most recent link
findings.description: It iterates the (key-sorted) map and keeps the last key, which is alphabetically last rather than most recently created.

findings.title: create() uses rand() for codes with no uniqueness check
findings.description: Codes are generated from std::rand() and assigned without collision detection, so a collision silently overwrites the existing link (and leaks quota accounting).

findings.title: Janitor erases from a std::map while iterating (UB)
findings.description: The loop calls store.all().erase(it) then ++it; it also mutates the store while other threads may access it, with no synchronization.

findings.title: stop_janitor() never joins or frees the thread
findings.description: It only sets the atomic flag and leaves g_janitor running/dangling, leaking the thread and its resources.

findings.title: warm_cache spawns detached threads that capture dangling references
findings.description: Threads capture &link (a loop-variable reference) and the vector is destroyed when warm_cache returns; threads are never joined, so they run against freed memory.

findings.title: check_targets iterates one past the end
findings.description: The loop condition i <= links.size() accesses links[links.size()], out of bounds.

findings.title: count_for_owner mutates the quota map when an owner is absent
findings.description: store.quotas()[owner] default-constructs a 0 entry, polluting the map via the non-const reference returned by quotas().

findings.title: Store::all() exposes the internal map for external mutation
findings.description: Callers (janitor included) can mutate/erase entries freely, breaking invariants and thread-safety; it is the enabler of the concurrency bugs above.

findings.title: Metrics::errors_ is uninitialized
findings.description: errors_ has no in-class initializer and no constructor sets it, so errors() returns an indeterminate value.
